tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay extending the prior C5-C7 K/P/G binding contract. The slice models a legitimate authorized transition from predecessor identity K/P1/G1 to successor payload P2 at G2, compares two protocols (A: reuse K with explicit predecessor binding and an atomic supersession record; B: allocate new logical key K2 linked to K/P1/G1), derives minimum atomic authorization/evidence fields, and falsifies one weak rule that treats a numerically higher generation as sufficient authorization. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

protocols.required_commit: atomically bind S1 and E2 to predecessor K/P1/G1 and successor K/P2/G2; mark predecessor superseded_by S1 and successor committed/authorized
protocols.exact_replay: same S1 + predecessor + successor reconstructs the committed transition without reissuing the effect
protocols.competing_successor: any different P/G or transition under reused K is a hard conflict unless it proves the same accepted S1 identity
protocols.tradeoff: preserves one logical key but makes every replay path check transition generation and predecessor binding before interpreting K

minimum_atomic_supersession_contract: Persist the exact predecessor identity {logical key, payload identity/digest, generation} that is eligible for replacement.
Persist the exact successor identity {logical key or new key, payload identity/digest, generation}; if a new key is used, persist an immutable supersedes link.
Bind a unique transition_id to an authority/fence epoch that explicitly authorizes this predecessor-to-successor transition.
Accept the transition only under an atomic precondition that the predecessor is still the authorized committed predecessor and has no different accepted successor.
Atomically persist predecessor->transition->successor evidence before interpreting later retries as duplicate-success.
Treat exact replay of the same transition identity as duplicate-success; treat any different successor, predecessor, or authority binding as conflict or unresolved rather than overwrite.
A generation number is ordering metadata, not authorization; legitimate advancement requires explicit predecessor and authority binding.

weak_supersession_rule.rule: For a logical effect family, accept any request carrying a numerically higher generation than the currently stored one and treat that as sufficient authorization to replace it.
falsification: A stale or competing worker can manufacture G3 after S1 without proving that K/P1/G1 or the accepted G2 successor is its authorized predecessor.
Generation ordering alone cannot distinguish a legitimate successor from a retry bug, payload mutation, or concurrent competing successor.
Both tested safe protocols require predecessor identity plus transition authority and an atomic no-other-successor precondition; W5 contains none of these fields.
Therefore higher-generation-wins can convert replay or concurrency drift into a second/mutated logical effect and fails the minimum C5-C7 supersession contract.

observations: Both compared protocols prevent retry/supersession confusion in the exact fixture only when the accepted transition binds predecessor, successor, transition identity and current authority under one atomic no-competing-successor condition.

Reusing K can be replay-safe but requires generation/transition interpretation on every lookup; allocating K2 keeps each idempotency identity immutable and moves generation advance into an explicit lineage edge.

A numerically larger generation cannot safely authorize mutation by itself because it carries no proof of which predecessor was current, who authorized the change, or whether another successor already won.
inference: For the exact abstract C5-C7 supersession replay tested, legitimate generation advance requires an explicit atomic transition contract, not merely a monotonic generation counter. The minimum evidence is predecessor identity, successor identity, unique transition id, current authority/fence binding, and an atomic no-other-successor precondition with durable predecessor->transition->successor readback. New-key lineage is structurally simpler to audit than same-key generation reuse in this fixture, but neither protocol is claimed to be implemented by any concrete Chat-exposed provider.
